scope: Only writer-local delivery/omission indexes and collector-owned event ID membership index. No runtime cache batching, compatibility aliases, privacy/projection changes, source configuration or service installation.

validation.elapsed_boundary: Synthetic test runtime only, not a production speed measurement.

archive_changes: Audit builds delivery_key -> event map while performing the existing duplicate-key check; trusted indexes enter state only after the unchanged audit succeeds.
Append batches reuse writer-local delivery and omission indexes, updating deliveries with each validated event. No trust is carried across lock lifetimes.
collector_changes: event_ids is built at initialization and rebuilt after archive synchronization.
event_ids is extended after ordinary committed capture, existing exact compatibility adoption and internal-session exclusion. These updates do not change the existing capture rules.
unchanged_guards: All-request validation before publication; causal parents and existing-key conflict checks.
Canonical publication functions and fsync behavior.
Poisoning after validation/publication failure; defensive returned-event copies; owner/thread/closed-writer checks.
Standalone per-source cursor-cache writes and derived cache recovery.
Existing narrow compatibility predicate and manifest validation, with no added aliases.
Source prefix/mutation checks, credential filtering and internal-session boundaries.

meaningful_cases: NoIteration guard forbids whole verified-record and omission rescans across repeated append batches under one audit.
Exact same-batch/cross-batch replay and conflicting delivery rejection with poisoned-writer protection.
Omitted delivery reservation remains enforced after a separate successful batch.
Partial publication cannot use in-memory unpublished delivery; reopen/re-audit recovers exact prior bytes.
Multiple standalone captures forbid full collector.events rescans and still write the durable derived cursor cache.
Forced archive synchronization discards stale membership IDs.
Compatibility adoption and internal exclusions update membership without new source-body reads or duplicate events.
New candidate signature reparses the synthetic frozen source with compatibility inactive while preserving old events/raw bytes.
Existing archive concurrency, corruption, prefix/mutation, view and capture regressions pass against candidate sources.

finding_resolved.issue: Initial regression runner preloaded candidate modules, but test_research_archive.py directly loaded the production file through a source-relative path.
finding_resolved.resolution: Eleven existing test files are exact copies under candidate/tests. Runner checks every loaded module path and separately verifies the direct archive loader SCRIPT/module.__file__ both target candidate.

remaining_boundaries: No production speedup or ETA is established. Startup audits, canonical fsyncs, whole cursor-cache writes and derived views still cost time.
Indexes occupy O(number of events) memory for the live writer/collector lifetime; this change removes repeated rebuilding, not archive size.
Changing the two signature files requires the root-authorized full replay. Old compatibility manifests fail their current-file checks; no new alias was introduced.
Installation, stopping/restarting the service, actual canonical replay and successor recovery/status receipt preparation remain root actions after review.
